newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defendant reverses witness position.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defendant reverses witness position.

text.p: In a surprise move, Oklahoma City bombing defendant Terry Nichols said Thursday he no longer opposed victim-witnesses attending his trial, bringing a sharp rebuke from his co-defendant's attorney.

"If any of the victims can get some peace of mind and/or relief of pain by personally sitting in court ... it's the least I can do in not opposing their right to view my trial," Nichols told a federal appeals court in a written statement.
Witnesses generally are not allowed to attend federal court proceedings before they testify in order to avoid influencing them.
Victims of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building bombing and the Justice Department have asked the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals to overturn the trial judge's ban on victims attending the trial.
The victims would testify at the penalty phase of the trial if the defendants are convicted. They would be allowed to describe the impact the bombing has had on their lives.
Nichols and co-defendant Timothy McVeigh, former army buddies, are awaiting separate trials in Denver for the April 1995 bombing, which resulted in 168 deaths.
Last month, Nichols' attorneys urged the appeals court to maintain the ban and Thursday's reversal was attacked by McVeigh's attorney Stephen Jones.
"Not for the first time has Terry Nichols tried to advance his interest at the expense of our client," Jones said. "This 'press release' should be seen for what it is."
Another McVeigh attorney, Robert Nigh, told Reuters: "Our position (in support of the ban) is not subject to change."
McVeigh is scheduled to go on trial March 31. No date has been set for Nichols.
